handoff_mode: single

debug: Verbose logging for cooldowns and locks. Until #176 this key was read
nowhere — setting it did nothing. Now: REMEMBER_DEBUG wins if set, then
this, then each script's own default (save-session verbose, git-backup
quiet). Remove the key entirely to keep those defaults.
haiku.oauth_token: OAuth token the plugin hands to the nested `claude -p` ONLY when the host
did not put CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN in the hook subprocess environment.
Some desktop / Agent-SDK hosts withhold it from spawned children, so the
summarization call is unauthenticated and nothing ever saves (#129/#131).
Create one with `claude setup-token`. The plugin holds this credential and
passes it to the CLI — set it deliberately. A host-provided token always
wins; the REMEMBER_OAUTH_TOKEN env var overrides this. Blank = disabled.
A malformed value (whitespace, under 20 chars, not a string) is refused
and reported in the daily log — it is never passed to the CLI.
consolidate_max_bytes: Skip-guard cap (UTF-8 bytes) on the assembled consolidation prompt
(staging + recent.md + archive.md). Default 600000. If the prompt would
exceed this, consolidation SKIPS that run (staging + memory left intact)
rather than overflowing Haiku's window with 'Prompt is too long' and
stalling all saves. Unlike extract_max_bytes the input is NOT truncated,
because consolidation rewrites recent/archive and truncating would drop
archived memory. Set 0 to disable the guard.
Since #346 the same number caps the OUTPUT too: a model response larger
than this is refused instead of being written to recent.md/archive.md.
Capping only the input meant one oversized response became the permanent
record AND pushed the store past this cap, so every later run skipped and
the file could never shrink again.
Since #348 a store already past this cap gets out again: whichever file
is measurably why the round will not fit is rotated to a dated sibling
and a fresh one started. Nothing is deleted and the slices are named at
session start. If the past-day staging files are over the cap on their
own, nothing is rotated — no rotation would change the next round.
staging_warn_bytes: Byte threshold (UTF-8) for a one-time WARNING when a today-*.md staging
file grows past it (#349). Staging files are append-only by design --
only a SUCCESSFUL consolidation round retires one -- so sustained lock
contention, a full disk, or a stalled consolidation (features.ndc_
compression off, or the #346 skip-forever state) leaves the same kind of
span appended every round with nothing to bound it. This does NOT cap or
truncate the file; it only logs (report_error, reaching hook-errors.log,
surfaced by /remember:doctor) the first time the file crosses the line,
so the growth is visible instead of silent. Set 0 to disable.
Default 2000000 -- comfortably above a healthy day's worth of staged
entries and comfortably below consolidate_max_bytes, so a warning here
is a signal something is stuck well before that separate skip-guard.
memory_inject_max_bytes: A memory file larger than this (UTF-8 bytes) is NAMED with its size at
session start instead of being cat'd into context. Default 200000.
The bytes stay on disk and stay greppable — what stops is pouring them
into a context window that cannot hold them. A healthy memory file is
kilobytes, so this only fires on a store that is already broken; in #346
a 6.4GB recent.md froze every `claude` launch in that project. Set 0 to
prompt_stamp: What the UserPromptSubmit hook injects into the model's context.
Two of the three fields in `full` change between turns for reasons that
have nothing to do with what you typed: the clock, and the context
percentage, which climbs on every prompt for anyone running the status
line. `stable` drops both and keeps the username. It KEEPS the >=95
context warning, which is threshold-gated and therefore only changes
bytes when it changes behaviour. `off` suppresses that warning too —
that is the difference between the two, and the reason both exist.
An unrecognised value is read as `full`.
model: Model for the summarize/consolidate calls (claude -p). Default 'haiku'.
Set 'sonnet' (or another tier) to improve salience + compression-cap
compliance; the call is backgrounded so there is no interactive cost.
An explicit REMEMBER_MODEL env var overrides this.
reject_pattern: Reject-gate regex keeping model refusals/clarifications out of memory.
'' -> the narrow built-in default (anchored refusal stems only).
'none' -> gate disabled (only the literal SKIP contract applies).
anything else -> a custom case-insensitive regex; invalid falls back to
the default. An explicit REMEMBER_REJECT_PATTERN env var overrides this.
handoff_mode: Two or more INTERACTIVE sessions share one project store by design
(_resolve_memory_project_dir, even across git worktrees, #56) -- but
the handoff note was always one fixed file, remember.md. The second
session's /remember silently overwrote the first's, which then
survived only in that session's own transcript, nowhere on disk (#363).
This is distinct from #221/#222: those protect a PENDING handoff from
a session that never writes one back; this is two sessions that each
DO write one, to the same name.
'single' (default, unchanged) -> every session shares remember.md,
exactly as before. The clobber is not fixed for an install that
never sets this key -- that trade is deliberate, matching every
other behaviour-changing key in this file (data_dir, reject_pattern,
git_restore.enabled): a new layout never applies until asked for.
'per_session' -> the handoff becomes remember.<session_id>.md, keyed
by the SessionStart payload's own session_id. History, recent.md,
archive.md and consolidation are untouched -- only the single
handoff slot is namespaced.
per_session needs a usable session_id to namespace anything. If none
reached the hook (the payload carried none, or it failed the #270
identifier sanitizer), the session falls back to the shared
remember.md -- the '=== HANDOFF ===' hint still points at it, since
that path is still correct (withholding the hint here broke external
storage mode, where it is the only real path), but a visible line
says the fallback happened so it does not read as isolation that
never applied. No pruning of stale remember.<session_id>.md files
ships with this key: the handoff is the user's own writing with no
copy anywhere else, and a delete keyed on "the transcript looks gone"
can misfire for reasons other than the transcript actually being
gone. Stale per-session handoffs accumulate until removed by hand.
git_backup.allow_remote_change: Guard against a swapped push remote. The backup hook records the remote
URL on the first push and aborts any later push whose URL differs — a
changed URL can mean a poisoned config.json pointing at an attacker's
host. false (default) keeps the guard on.
Set true only to deliberately re-point at a new repo; the next push
records the new URL, so set it back to false afterwards.
Note: before the jq-free config fallback landed, machines without jq
always read this as false regardless of configuration. It is now honoured
there too, so an existing true in your config takes effect on those
hooks.dispatch_timeout_seconds: How long ONE hooks.d/ listener may take before it is stopped. Nothing
bounded them until #286: dispatch() runs them in the foreground, so one
that blocks stalled the agent for as long as it blocked and logged
Two numbers, because two kinds of caller wait on this and only one of
them is a person. The interactive one covers after_post_tool,
after_user_prompt and both session_start events; the detached one covers
before/after_save and before/after_consolidate, dispatched from a nohup'd
process nobody is waiting on. Claude Code kills a hook at 60s by default,
so an interactive budget at or above that is the host killing the process
The shipped listeners take 0.17-0.58s in the foreground (their git I/O is
in a disowned subshell and does not count), so these are ~25x and ~200x
headroom. Set 0 to disable the bound.
The kill is SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after dispatch_kill_grace_seconds, so a
listener that traps EXIT gets to release its lock. It is a courtesy, not
a veto: one that traps TERM and keeps going is killed anyway. The signal
goes to the listener's own PID, never its process group — a listener's
disowned background work is deliberately left running.
data_dir: Controls where memory data files are stored.
External mode — absolute or home-relative path:
{slug} is replaced by the same slug Claude Code uses for
~/.claude/projects/<slug>/, so each project gets its own
isolated subtree. The .gitignore is NOT written in external
mode — manage the ~/.remember/ tree as your own private repo.
User-global config lives at ~/.remember/config.json and is
merged on top of this file (per-project overrides user-global
which overrides these shipped defaults). See config.user.example.json.
